summary: The chart for "Frère Jacques" (57.5 s, 95.7 bpm, 4/4) is in F major and the chord histogram agrees: F dominates (59 beats), C follows (27), and the only other chord is the single A# segment, which is simply Bb misspelled — the key has no A#, so c006 is respelled to Bb (and re-affirmed as a plain triad). No blips needed merging: the 1–2 beat F/C alternations (c002–c007, c011–c012, c015–c016, c019–c020) are the song's actual two-chord oscillation, not misdetections, and no out-of-key chords remain. For beginners the song uses only F, C, Bb, so capo 5 with C shapes yields C, G and F — all open chords — and a simple "D-DU-UDU" strum fits the steady nursery-rhyme pulse. The form is labelled as a 14-beat instrumental intro (c001), the first stanza as verse 1 (l003–l008), an identical repeat as verse 2 (l009–l015, same F-C-F pattern as the first), and the final "Ding dang dong" plus 4-beat F cadence as the outro. Lyrics are correct and complete with no line-break problems; only l013 and l014 ("Sonnez les matines") show compressed timing (min unit ~0.30–0.31 s vs 0.6 s elsewhere) and were flagged rather than edited.
